title: Flavipin from fungi as a potential inhibitor of rheumatoid arthritis signaling molecules.
authors: Ahmed, Emad A; Alzahrani, Abdulaah M; Abdelsalam, Salah A; Ibrahim, Hairul-Islam M
one_liner_zh: 该文研究真菌代谢物Flavipin对类风湿关节炎信号分子的抑制，涉及TNF-alpha和JAK的分子对接与MD模拟，但对象为蛋白-小分子互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA体系，仅方法可部分借鉴。
abstract: Flavipin, a fungal lower molecular weight biomolecule (MW 196.16 g/mol), has not been yet extensively studied for beneficial preclinical and clinical applications. In recent years, various preclinical mouse models including adjuvant-induced arthritis (AIA) were employed to understand mechanisms associated with Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and to develop new therapeutic drugs. In the current study, we studied the inhibitory effect of Flavipin on major signaling molecules involved in the inflammatory response during RA using both in-silico virtual interaction and in vivo mouse model of AIA. Our in-silico results clarified that Flavipin interacts with the tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-alpha) through conventional hydrogen binding (H-H) at one of TNF-alpha critical amino acids tyrosine residues, Tyr119, with binding energy (b.e.) -5.9. In addition, Flavipin binds to ATP-binging sites of the Jesus kinases, JAK1, JAK2 and JAK3, through H-H (b. e. between -5.8 and -6.1) and then it may inhibit JAKs, regulators of RA signaling molecules. Moreover, our molecular dynamics stimulation for the docked TNF-alpha/Flavipin complex confirmed the specificity and the stability of the interaction. In vitro, Flavipin is not toxic to normal cells at doses below 50 microM (its IC50 in normal fibroblast cell line was above 100 microM). However, in vivo, the arthritis score and hind paw oedema parameters were modulated in Flavipin treated mice. Consistent with the in-silico results the levels of the TNF-alpha, the nuclear transcription factor kappaB (NF-kappaB) and the signal transduction and activator of transcription (STAT3, downstream of JAKs) were modulated at joint tissues of the hind-paw of Flavipin/AIA treated mice. Our data suggest Flavipin as a potential therapeutic agent for arthritis can inhibit RA major signaling molecules.
abstract_zh: Flavipin，一种真菌来源的低分子量生物分子（分子量196.16 g/mol），迄今尚未在临床前及临床应用方面得到广泛研究。近年来，多种临床前小鼠模型，包括佐剂诱导性关节炎（AIA），被用于理解类风湿性关节炎（RA）的相关机制并开发新的治疗药物。在本研究中，我们通过计算机虚拟相互作用和AIA小鼠体内模型，研究了Flavipin对RA炎症反应中主要信号分子的抑制作用。我们的计算机模拟结果表明，Flavipin通过常规氢键（H-H）与肿瘤坏死因子α（TNF-alpha）相互作用，结合位点位于TNF-alpha关键氨基酸酪氨酸残基Tyr119，结合能（b.e.）为-5.9。此外，Flavipin通过H-H（b.e.在-5.8至-6.1之间）与Jesus激酶JAK1、JAK2和JAK3的ATP结合位点结合，从而可能抑制JAKs，这些是RA信号分子的调节因子。进一步，我们对对接的TNF-alpha/Flavipin复合物进行的分子动力学模拟确认了该相互作用的特异性和稳定性。在体外实验中，Flavipin在低于50微摩尔浓度下对正常细胞无毒性（其在正常成纤维细胞系中的IC50超过100微摩尔）。然而，在体内实验中，Flavipin处理的小鼠关节炎评分和后爪水肿参数得到调节。与计算机模拟结果一致，Flavipin/AIA处理小鼠后爪关节组织中TNF-alpha、核转录因子kappaB（NF-kappaB）及信号转导和转录激活因子3（STAT3，JAKs下游）的水平得到调节。我们的数据表明，Flavipin作为关节炎的潜在治疗剂，能够抑制RA的主要信号分子。
